text:
ash: FYI a customer reported ~5% of hosted-api requests getting 502s only when sending streaming/chunked bodies. Happening in us-east-1, started ~0300 UTC. trace_id=trc_8f3a2b
jamie: are these h2 or http/1.1 clients? any client examples?
ash: http/1.1 mostly; client is using Transfer-Encoding: chunked. They said if they send the same payload with Content-Length set, errors disappear.
maria: that points at edge/Envoy upstream_reset_before_response_started or connection reset on write. can you paste a sample envoy log line?
ash: pasted relevant lines below (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:15.123Z] proxy[out] req=trc_8f3a2b path=/v1/generate upstream=10.2.5.43:8080 reset: reason=connection_failure, details=reset_before_response_started
[2026-03-16T03:12:15.124Z] http1: client->edge keepalive=1 chunked=true content-length=none
```
evian (infra-bot): noticed increased RST_STREAM from upstream during chunked body streaming around that window. rolling window shows TCP retransmits spike for that host pool.
jamie: can we repro locally with curl using chunked transfer? try:
```bash
printf '10\nhellohello\n0\n\n' | curl -v -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' --data-binary @- https://api.hosted.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
ash: tried that and got 502 from edge ~40% of runs on my laptop. when I set `-H 'Content-Length: 10'` it succeeds consistently.
maria: interesting. This smells like backend (model runner) closing connection early when receiving chunked body? but we also see envoy upstream reset. Need full traces (edge request id + worker id). ash can you grab the request-id header and the host header from a failing run?
ash: sample headers from fail: `x-request-id: trc_8f3a2b`, `x-edge-host: pool-us-east-1-gpu-12`
jamie: pinging eng-runtime to look for worker-side logs for pool gpu-12 at that timestamp. tagged @evan-fyi.
ev an: I'll grep the worker logs. quick note — our runners expect Content-Length for streaming ingest path; chunked is supported but we recently landed a patch that changes how we drain read buffers under backpressure. putting that together now.
maria: short-term mitigation options for customers: 1) set Content-Length, 2) disable chunked in client (send buffered), 3) route to Dedicated (different pool) as workaround.
ash: passed mitigation steps to customer; they want a more seamless fix.
jamie: runtime eng — if worker change is root cause, can we make edge detect chunked->buffer then set Content-Length header before forwarding? (cheap shim)
ev an: possible but brittle. safer fix is fix runner read loop to tolerate chunked with intermittent small frames. patch incoming, I'll drop a link once CI passes.
maria: also track this as a regression candidate — we had a kernel-level change in 02/2026 that touched socket recv semantics on our runtime AMI. evan pls confirm.
ev an: confirmed patch notes reference `MSG_WAITALL` change; that could interact with chunked decoding. investigating.
ash: customer asked for repro steps to test their side — shared the curl snippet above and suggested `--no-keepalive` to force new TCP connections. they reported lower failure rate but still see flakes.
jamie: capture tcpdump next time: `sudo tcpdump -i any host <edge-ip> and tcp port 443 -w chunked.pcap` and attach. also enable `x-debug: full` header so we get edge trace dump.
maria: logging action: create support ticket, assign to eng-runtime, include trace_id trc_8f3a2b and worker pool. set priority=P1 for customer SLA.
ash: created ticket #SUP-4821 and added logs + traces. cc @evan.
ev an: pushed a runtime branch that tweaks read loop and adds more defensive handling for EOF during chunked frames. I'll run nightly canary against us-east-1 pool and report back.
jamie: thanks. once canary passes, we can do a small edge filter that normalizes chunked->content-length for a short window to reduce customer pain.
ash: customer notified (they said thanks and will try Content-Length workaround for now). will update thread when eng confirms fix. :thumbsup:
